title: Divergent Change (Multi-Role Structs)
pattern: A single class or struct that is constantly modified for completely unrelated business reasons (such as changing a tax rate formula AND updating a PDF layout format).
why_bad: Direct violation of the Single Responsibility Principle. The struct is highly fragile; changing the PDF layout code can introduce compilation or logic errors that break core tax calculation routines. It forces extensive re-testing of the entire class for unrelated changes, increasing code friction.
detection: Observe a single source file being modified under disparate, unrelated commit headings (e.g., "Fix PDF layout" and "Fix tax brackets") over time.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. Centralized system dispatchers or routers that act purely as structural links and naturally touch multiple parts of the application, although they should still contain no actual business logic.
fix: Split the struct into smaller, highly cohesive, single-purpose structs (e.g., `TaxCalculator`, `InvoiceRenderer`, and `OrderRepository`).
source: *Martin Fowler - Refactoring (1999)*, Chapter 3, "Divergent Change"; *Sandi Metz - Practical Object-Oriented Design (2019)*, Chapter 2.
